analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1239-1677) covering historical release entries. The PR's changed range is the document head, where a v0.10.4 candidate section is added. That section appears only as a truncated patch excerpt, and its lines are not visible in the supplied base-side units. I therefore cannot cite or evaluate it on the head side. The excerpt is documentation only. It touches no executable code, authorization logic, key handling, attestation, cache storage or WebSocket handling.

The visible patch text mentions Qwen JSON response_format changes, grammar-constrained output that can turn truncation into a 422 `tool_noncompliance`, forced `tool_choice` advertisement through `tool_constraint_models`, and a `prompt_anchor_mismatch` cache-receipt quarantine during a provider/coordinator version skew. These are described as documented behaviors of other changes, not as code in this diff. Cache affinity quarantine for up to 10 minutes is an availability and rollout concern that is mitigated by every request still being served. It is relevant to T-041 and TB-002 only as context.

The base excerpt reaffirms existing posture. Encrypted SSD checkpoint eviction no longer rotates routing epochs, and FIFO substitution is rejected. Neither is a claim about new code in this PR. The T-041 definition already records that the epoch is a routing-evidence generation and not a purge primitive.

No regressions or new attack surface can be established from this evidence. Remaining question: the full v0.10.4 candidate text and the corresponding code changes, which are outside this batch. If the PR carries code changes in other batches, those need separate review against T-041, TB-007 and TB-002. The documentation-only content here cannot support a security conclusion about them.
